answer: An agent economy resists sybil attacks via bonded identity. Every agent posts a stake, a pearl of capital locked while active, and spends a plume of it per interaction, so fake agents burn real money to act. Behavioral fingerprinting groups duplicates; once a sybil cluster is proven, each fake agent's pearl is slashed and given to honest ones. A long-lived honest agent earns a lotus of reputation that lowers its fees. For an attacker, each fake identity costs scarce capital up front and risks total loss, while the lotus of trust cannot be forged cheaply, so the economy favors genuine agents.
